answer: Each identity needs sponsor endorsement and a 60-credit bond in the jade registry. A sponsor holds one 300-credit pool, split equally among identities, so weight is 300 over that count. Auditors map endorsements into a trellis graph, recomputing weights at the opal checkpoint. At the 100-weight threshold a sponsor carries three, so the k-th fake past each trio needs a new 200-credit sponsor; 1,000 fakes cost 126,800. A rented-sponsor ring fails when the trellis exposes its fan-out and one proven fake slashes the pool. An honest agent pays 60 once and keeps full weight.
